summary: CI now runs the Go race detector nightly (and on demand via workflow_dispatch), which nothing in the repo had ever done. The first run found three data races. The real one is in mypintusan's door controller: DoorMachine's fields were unsynchronized across the goroutines that drive it, because Controller.mu only ever guarded the MAP of machines and is released before tickDoors calls Tick — so an operator hitting the lockdown endpoint (apis/doors.go) mutated the same machine the bus goroutine was ticking. Losing a shuntUntil write raises a forced-door alarm on a legitimate entry; losing a contactOpen write means a forced door never alarms at all. DoorMachine now carries its own mutex and takes it in every exported method, returning events only after the lock is dropped so emitDoorEvents cannot re-enter under it. The other two were test-infrastructure races that would have made the new nightly permanently red: myseliasan's fakeSettingsRepo is now mutex-guarded, and infra/safego's captureLogs returns a locked snapshot function instead of a bare pointer to the slice its logger goroutine appends to.
compatibility: Backward compatible. No API, config or schema changes. The race job is nightly rather than per-PR because the instrumented build is several times slower and a check that doubles PR latency gets worked around; CGO_ENABLED is 1 in that job only (the race detector requires cgo) while the existing build job keeps CGO off to match the static release builds. Scope is deliberately "core" alone even though the DoorMachine fix is an app-level bug in mypintusan: mypintusan has no entry in infra/versioning/version.json yet, and the bump tool treats an unknown scope token as a hard error (verified — "core,mypintusan" fails the pipeline). mypintusan therefore has no release channel to tag; the fix ships with its first release, whenever version.json gains that app.
